messages:
lina_support: FYI -- customer AcmeReports reporting intermittent 500s + weird top-ranked items from /v1/rerank. Happening on ~0.6% of requests, mostly when inputs include emoji clusters or pasted content from Slack/Teams. I attached a minimal payload in the ticket.

jamal_infra: Can you paste the payload snippet here? I want to grep logs.

lina_support: Sure, here's the example they say reproduces 500s 100% of the time: 
```json
{
  "query": "summarize:\u0000 quarterly results 🧾\uDBFF\uDFFF",
  "documents": ["Revenue up 12%\u0000", "Net margin stable 👍\ud83d"]
}
```
They included literal null bytes (\u0000) and some broken surrogate pairs from copy/paste.

marta_eng: Ugh. Server logs show a UTF decode on the reranker worker: 
```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 14: invalid start byte
  File "/app/reranker/inputs.py", line 78, in parse_request
    text = raw_bytes.decode('utf-8')
```
Looks like some edges aren't being sanitized in the HTTP ingress.

oli_product: Does this explain the odd scores too? Customer says some documents get extremely high rerank scores when payload had these chars.

marta_eng: Possibly. If tokenization falls back or misaligns when invalid bytes slip through, model input mismatch could produce garbage logits or push a fallback model path. Also saw a short stack trace referencing tokenization normalization.

jamal_infra: Quick mitigation: routing rules can drop to 200ms cached responses for that customer while we patch. But we should patch the ingest sanitizer. Best short-term fix is to reject payloads with control chars (400) and include helpful message about cleaning.

lina_support: Customer doesn't want 400s; they want automatic handling. Asked for ETA.

marta_eng: Plan: add a pre-tokenizer pass to strip/replace \u0000 and unpaired surrogates, normalize to NFC, and log a sanitized hash for debugging. Will add a canary flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in. I can push a quick PR to the reranker worker to run: 
```py
# naive sanitizer (canary)
def sanitize_text(s):
    import unicodedata, re
    s = s.replace('\x00', '\uFFFD')
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)
    s = re.sub(r'[\u0000-\u001F\u007F]', '', s)
    return s
```
This should prevent the decode error and reduce tokenization surprises.

jamal_infra: Also add unit tests with grapheme clusters and emoji ZWJ sequences and some malformed UTF-8 blobs. I'll add a quick integration test that pumps the exact payload through the canonical tokenizer container.

oli_product: Customer asked for a rollback-safe deploy. Can we utter a canary + metrics for rerank-error-rate, mean top-score, and a sample of sanitized inputs?

marta_eng: Yes. Will emit metrics: rerank.sanitizer.applied, rerank.sanitizer.rejected, rerank.sanitizer.replaced_chars. Hook them into Console and alert if sanitizer applied > 0.1% for a tenant.

ingest-bot: ticket#IN-4829 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IN-4829 -- assignee marta_eng, priority P2. Logs and test vector attached.

lina_support: Sending customer interim note: "We're rolling a small canary sanitizer to reduce failures; please keep sending examples if you see odd scores." They want ETA end of day tomorrow.

marta_eng: I'll try to get the PR up today, tests + canary tomorrow EOD. If we hit weird tokenization regressions, we may need to pin the reranker model variant for this tenant while we iterate.

jamal_infra: I'll reserve a canary pod pool and ensure metrics pipeline picks up the new metrics. Also adding a log hook to capture pre/post sanitized pair for a sample of requests (PII scrubbed).

lina_support: Thanks all. If the customer reports any specific payloads, drop them here (no PII).

oli_product: One follow-up: could this be caused upstream by our JS SDK double-encoding emoji clusters? We should grep client SDKs too.

marta_eng: Good call. Adding a quick job to scan recent request bodies for suspicious byte sequences and SDK user-agent strings.

lina_support: Closing loop: customer acknowledged and will monitor. Will reopen thread if they see new failures. :thumbsup:
